title: Minimize host copy churn with reusable staging arenas and adaptive worker throttling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Host-side overhead during model priming (prefetch/priming to GPU) and decoding is a dominant contributor to p50/p95 latency spikes for short-to-medium sequences. Symptoms include repeated allocations of pinned pages, scatter/gather memory choreographies that amplify memcpy fanout, and threadpool contention when many lightweight requests concurrently race to stage KV/prefill buffers. This ticket proposes a two-pronged approach: 1) a reusable per-GPU staging arena and DMA resource pool to eliminate per-request pinned allocations and reduce copy fanout, and 2) adaptive worker throttling (a backpressure mechanism for host worker threads) to reduce thread wake contention and flatten CPU utilization while preserving latency SLOs.
design_decision_summary: We will implement a fixed-size ring of reusable pinned-memory arenas per GPU that are recycled by a lightweight ownership token. Arena sizes are configurable by model profile and sequence-length buckets. Transfers will use a scatter-merge step on the host to coalesce small host buffers into a single DMA scatter-gather descriptor when possible. The host threadpool will be augmented with an adaptive throttler: workers take a lease token (with a short TTL) before performing heavy staging work; when the lease queue is saturated the scheduler will apply exponential backoff and drop low-priority background prefetches. Kernel selector will expose a 'staging-friendly' hint so certain quantized kernels can accept already-coalesced host buffers and skip extra copies. This keeps changes minimally invasive to runtime and gives rapid rollback paths.
benchmark_goals: Reduce host CPU cycles attributable to staging and memcpy by >=35% on mixed short-tail workloads. Improve end-to-end p95 latency for 16-128 token requests by >=10ms in our microbench harness. Maintain throughput within 5% of baseline for heavy BATCH workloads.
implementation_notes:
- per-gpu arenas: allocate at init time from a shared pinned page pool; arenas are slab-like: multiple slices of equal size to avoid fragmentation.
- lease-based ownership: lock-free ring index plus atomic state transition to avoid expensive mutexes.
- scatter-merge pass: apply heuristics to only merge when total contiguous size < merge_threshold and number_of_fragments > min_frag_count.
- adaptive throttling: measure worker wake rate and CPU contention; throttle low-value prefetch requests first (configured via label).
- kernel hinting: add small flag in kernel launch path; do not change public API surface.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Arena size misconfiguration could lead to OOM. Mitigation: start with conservative default sizes per model family and add runtime eviction metrics + auto-tuner. Risk: Throttling may increase tail latency for some background-critical workloads. Mitigation: priority labels and emergency bypass for high-SLA routes; A/B feature gated rollout. Risk: merging step could hurt throughput for very large scatter lists. Mitigation: threshold heuristics and disable merge for >N fragments.
comments: 2025-07-15 - Aisha Patel: Initial discovery showed repeated calls to posix_memalign + mlock in the hot path when staging KV caches. Captured flamegraphs and a heap profile attached to the Confluence doc.

2025-07-21 - Marco Liu: Prototype of per-GPU arena allocator implemented and benchmarked on dev-box. Synthetic microbench shows 28% CPU savings for small requests (<=32 tokens). Observed one pathological case where arena recycling collided with prefetch retries - added lease TTL to mitigate.

2025-07-28 - Design review notes (PM/Infra): PM requested explicit flow for dedicated vs hosted modes (dedicated can allocate larger arenas). Infra asked to ensure KMS/HSM key operations are not performed while stalls hold arenas - we scoped those calls out of the lease-critical path.
2025-07-30 - PR opened: runtime/pull/1287 containing allocator + throttler and unit tests. Running internal e2e job #staging-arena-e2e-4.

2025-08-02 - Benchmark update: End-to-end harness (chat-sim load) shows p95 improvement of 12.3ms and median CPU cycles reduction of ~33% for host staging. Throughput at 95th percentile load within 3% of baseline. Still need longer soak on Dedicated pools.

2025-08-02 - Next: add telemetry for arena occupancy by model, expose admin API to adjust arena sizes per-customer, and schedule a canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic before promoting to Dedicated staging.
2025-08-02 - Reviewer note (SRE): Please add automated alerts for arena exhaustion and a graceful fallback to the old allocation path to avoid hard failures in canary.
2025-08-02 - Security note: Confirmed no secret material touches the staging arenas; security review flagged and closed for this work.
2025-08-02 - QA checklist: regression tests for stream-in chunking, kernel-hint correctness, and prefetch bypass when throttling engaged.
